issues.description: Transitive() drops the last entry unconditionally, ignoring whether descriptor.proto is actually implicit.
issues.detail: ir_imports.go uses `files[:max(0, len(i.files)-1)]` with a comment 'Exclude the implicit descriptor.proto.' No invariant is stated proving the last element is always descriptor.proto. If imports is empty after the zero-guard, the slice is `nil[:0]` which is fine, but for a populated imports where descriptor.proto is not present, this silently drops a legitimate transitive import. State the invariant or check.

issues.description: Reflection-based test treats any method with no non-receiver inputs as an 'accessor', which is unsound.
issues.detail: testZeroAny iterates ty.NumMethod() and calls anything with NumIn()==1. This will invoke mutators, finalizers, or side-effecting methods named e.g. Close, Reset, Finalize if any exist now or later. The invariant 'no-arg method == pure accessor' is not stated and is fragile. Filter by naming convention or an explicit accessor registry, or document the assumption.

issues.description: Special-casing ValueNodeIndex by method name hides a design smell — sentinel -1 is undocumented in the type contract.
issues.detail: The test hardcodes the name 'ValueNodeIndex' to expect -1. A sentinel return value for zero is the kind of thing that needs a stated invariant on the method itself, not embedded in a generic test. The doc comment says '-1 if empty' but callers must still defend. Consider returning (int, bool) or documenting the sentinel on Element more loudly.

issues.description: Repeated `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field }; return makeIndexer(x, ...)` pattern is begging for a helper.
issues.detail: The same six-line incantation appears ~12 times in ir_file.go and ir_type.go. A small helper like `nilSafeSlice(f, func(f *File) []T { return f.types })` or methods on a niladic receiver would compress this to one line and make the invariant ('zero file yields empty indexer') stateable once. Current form is correct but unreadable in aggregate; literate-comment grade is low.

issues.description: AllMembers iterator increments `i` outside the nil-guarded branch, but the closure still captures a possibly-zero seq.
issues.detail: When f is nil, `raw` is the zero iter.Seq which yields nothing, so `i` never increments — fine. But this is non-obvious. A one-line comment stating 'nil file -> empty iterator, i unused' would let a reader verify termination and emptiness without re-deriving it. Same applies to most of the new nil-branches: the invariant is correct but unstated.

issues.description: Inconsistent guard style: some methods check `f == nil`, others build a zero local `imp` and call through it.
issues.detail: IsDescriptorProto early-returns on `f == nil`; Imports/TransitiveImports construct a zero `imports` and dispatch. Both terminate, but the choice is ad hoc. Pick one convention and apply it: early-return for scalar results, zero-local-dispatch for indexers — and document why. Otherwise future readers will not know which pattern is canonical when adding new accessors.

review.summary: RIGOROUS in intent, UNDER-AUDITED in execution. The PR systematically hardens zero-value accessors and adds a reflective test harness — a worthy goal. Three concerns: the Transitive() 'minus one for descriptor.proto' lacks a stated invariant and may now silently drop legitimate imports when the assumption fails; the reflective test treats every no-arg method as a pure accessor, which is unsound as a forward-compatible contract; and the repeated `var x; if f != nil { x = f.field }` pattern wants a NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT helper since it appears a dozen times. The sentinel -1 from ValueNodeIndex deserves louder documentation. None of these block merge, but the loop-invariants should be written down before the next reader inherits this code.
